sections.subtopic: 04 · Graphs and Periodicity of Trigonometric Functions
sections.title: A graph is the unit circle, unrolled

board_events.text: Unrolling the circle into a wave
Walk anticlockwise round the unit circle and plot your height, sin x, against the distance walked. The height traces a wave.

board_events.caption: y = sin x: the unit circle's height unrolled along a line

board_events.text: Height rises to $+1$ at $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, back to $0$ at $\pi$, down to $-1$ at $\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$, and $0$ again at $2\pi$.
Periodicity — the pattern that repeats

board_events.latex: f(x+T)=f(x),\quad T\ \text{the smallest such positive number}

board_events.text: Sine and cosine repeat every full turn, $T=2\pi$. Tangent repeats every half turn, $T=\pi$.
Tangent depends on the line's direction, which looks 'the same' after 180° — hence period π.

segments.text: A graph turns trigonometry from something you compute into something you can see.

Here's the trick: walk anticlockwise around the unit circle, and at each angle x plot your height, which is sine x, against the distance you've walked. That height, laid out along a line, is the sine wave.
This is it. The wave is literally the circle's up-coordinate, unrolled.

Follow the height: it rises to plus one at pi over two, drops back to zero at pi, dips to minus one at three pi over two, and returns to zero at two pi. Then a new lap begins and the whole shape repeats.
That repetition has a name, periodicity.
A function is periodic with period capital T if f of x plus T always equals f of x, and T is the smallest positive number that works.
Sine and cosine repeat every full turn, so their period is two pi. Tangent, though, repeats every half turn, its period is pi.
Why only pi for tangent? Tangent measures the direction of the line through the origin, and a line points the same way again after just one hundred eighty degrees.
Graph trigonometry को compute करने वाली चीज़ से देखने वाली चीज़ बना देता है.
Trick ये है: unit circle के around anticlockwise चलिए, और हर angle x पर अपनी height, यानी sine x, को चली हुई distance के against plot कीजिए. वो height, एक line पर बिछी हुई, sine wave है.
ये रहा. Wave literally circle की up-coordinate है, unrolled.
Height follow कीजिए: pi over two पर plus one तक चढ़ती है, pi पर वापस zero, three pi over two पर minus one तक गिरती है, और two pi पर फिर zero. फिर नया lap शुरू, पूरी shape repeat.
इस repetition का नाम है periodicity.
एक function periodic है period capital T के साथ अगर f of x plus T हमेशा f of x के बराबर हो, और T सबसे छोटा positive number जो काम करे.
Sine और cosine हर full turn पर repeat होते हैं, so period two pi. पर tangent हर half turn पर repeat होता है, इसका period pi.
Tangent के लिए pi ही क्यों? Tangent origin से गुज़रती line की direction नापता है, और line सिर्फ़ one hundred eighty degrees बाद फिर same तरफ़ point करती है.
Graph trigonometry को गणना करने वाली चीज़ से देखने वाली चीज़ बना देता है.
युक्ति यह है: unit circle के चारों ओर anticlockwise चलिए, और हर angle x पर अपनी height, यानी sine x, को चली हुई distance के सामने plot कीजिए. वह height, एक line पर बिछी हुई, sine wave है.
यह रहा. Wave सचमुच circle की up-coordinate है, unrolled.
Height का पीछा कीजिए: pi बटा two पर plus one तक चढ़ती है, pi पर वापस zero, three pi बटा two पर minus one तक गिरती है, और two pi पर फिर zero. फिर नया lap शुरू, पूरी आकृति दोहराई जाती है.
इस दोहराव का नाम है periodicity.
एक function periodic है period capital T के साथ अगर f of x plus T हमेशा f of x के बराबर हो, और T सबसे छोटी धनात्मक संख्या जो काम करे.
Sine और cosine हर full turn पर दोहराते हैं, तो period two pi. पर tangent हर half turn पर दोहराता है, इसका period pi.
Tangent के लिए pi ही क्यों? Tangent origin से गुज़रती line की दिशा नापता है, और line सिर्फ़ one hundred eighty degrees बाद फिर उसी ओर संकेत करती है.

sections.subtopic: 04 · Graphs and Periodicity of Trigonometric Functions
sections.title: Stretching and shifting — what a, b, c, d do

board_events.text: Reading y = a·sin(bx + c) + d
$|a|$ stretches vertically \u2014 the amplitude, how tall the wave is.
$b$ squeezes horizontally \u2014 bigger $b$ means more oscillations, so a shorter period.

board_events.caption: sin x vs 2 sin x (taller) vs sin 2x (twice as fast)

board_events.text: $c$ slides the wave left or right \u2014 a phase shift. $d$ lifts the whole wave up or down.
Range becomes [d − |a|, d + |a|] — the vertical shift moves the whole band.

segments.text: One template covers every sine and cosine you'll meet: y equals a sine of b x plus c, all plus d.
The size of a stretches the wave vertically. That's the amplitude, how tall the peaks are.
The b squeezes it horizontally. A bigger b packs in more oscillations in the same space, which means a shorter period.
See it here: compared to plain sine x, the red curve two sine x is twice as tall, and the green curve sine two x oscillates twice as fast.
The c slides the wave sideways, a phase shift, and d lifts the whole wave up or down.
So amplitude is the size of a, period is two pi over the size of b, and the vertical shift is d.
And crucially, the range becomes d minus the size of a, up to d plus the size of a. The shift d moves the entire band, don't forget it.
एक template हर sine और cosine को cover करता है: y equals a sine of b x plus c, पूरे में plus d.
a का size wave को vertically stretch करता है. यही amplitude है, peaks कितने ऊँचे.
b इसे horizontally squeeze करता है. बड़ा b same space में ज़्यादा oscillations भरता है, यानी छोटा period.
यहाँ देखिए: plain sine x के मुक़ाबले, red curve two sine x दुगुना ऊँचा है, और green curve sine two x दुगनी तेज़ी से oscillate करता है.
c wave को sideways slide करता है, phase shift, और d पूरी wave को ऊपर या नीचे उठाता है.
So amplitude है a का size, period है two pi over b का size, और vertical shift है d.
और ज़रूरी बात, range बनता है d minus a का size, से d plus a का size तक. Shift d पूरी band हिला देता है, इसे मत भूलिए.
एक template हर sine और cosine को cover करता है: y बराबर a sine of b x plus c, पूरे में plus d.
a का आकार wave को vertically खींचता है. यही amplitude है, peaks कितने ऊँचे.
b इसे horizontally दबाता है. बड़ा b उसी जगह में ज़्यादा oscillations भरता है, यानी छोटा period.
यहाँ देखिए: सादे sine x के मुक़ाबले, red curve two sine x दुगुना ऊँचा है, और green curve sine two x दुगनी तेज़ी से oscillate करता है.
c wave को अगल-बगल खिसकाता है, phase shift, और d पूरी wave को ऊपर या नीचे उठाता है.
तो amplitude है a का आकार, period है two pi बटा b का आकार, और vertical shift है d.
और ज़रूरी बात, range बनता है d minus a का आकार, से d plus a का आकार तक. Shift d पूरी band हिला देता है, इसे मत भूलिए.

sections.title: Periods, the scaling rule and the transform summary

board_events.text: Base periods of the six functions

board_events.latex: \sin x,\ \cos x,\ \sec x,\ \csc x:\ T=2\pi\qquad \tan x,\ \cot x:\ T=\pi

board_events.caption: y = tan x: period π, vertical asymptotes at odd multiples of π/2

board_events.text: Special composites

board_events.latex: |\sin x|,\ |\cos x|,\ \sin^2 x,\ \cos^2 x:\ T=\pi;\quad \text{sum} \Rightarrow \text{LCM of periods}

board_events.text: Asymptotes: $\tan,\sec$ blow up where $\cos=0$ (odd $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$); $\cot,\csc$ where $\sin=0$ ($n\pi$).

segments.text: Here is the full reference you need to read or sketch any trig graph.
Base periods: sine, cosine, secant and cosecant all repeat over two pi; tangent and cotangent repeat over pi.
The scaling rule: the period of a function of b x plus c is the base period divided by the size of b. The constant c only shifts the graph, it never changes the period.
Here's the tangent graph to fix those ideas: period pi between branches, with vertical asymptotes at the odd multiples of pi over two, wherever cosine is zero.
Now the composites that trip students.

The absolute values of sine and cosine, and sine squared and cosine squared, all have period pi, not two pi. And for a sum of functions, the period is the least common multiple of the individual periods.
For asymptotes: tangent and secant blow up where cosine is zero, the odd multiples of pi over two; cotangent and cosecant blow up where sine is zero, the whole multiples of pi.

And the master transform line: for a sine of b x plus c, all plus d, amplitude is the size of a, period is two pi over the size of b, phase shift is minus c over b, and range is d minus the size of a to d plus the size of a.
किसी भी trig graph को पढ़ने या sketch करने का पूरा reference यहाँ है.
Base periods: sine, cosine, secant और cosecant सब two pi पर repeat; tangent और cotangent pi पर repeat.
Scaling rule: function of b x plus c का period है base period divided by b का size. Constant c सिर्फ़ graph shift करता है, period कभी नहीं बदलता.
उन ideas को fix करने के लिए tangent graph: branches के बीच period pi, vertical asymptotes odd multiples of pi over two पर, जहाँ cosine zero है.
अब वो composites जहाँ students फँसते हैं.
Sine और cosine के absolute values, और sine squared और cosine squared, सबका period pi है, two pi नहीं. और functions के sum के लिए, period है individual periods का least common multiple.
Asymptotes के लिए: tangent और secant वहाँ blow up होते हैं जहाँ cosine zero है, odd multiples of pi over two; cotangent और cosecant वहाँ जहाँ sine zero है, pi के whole multiples.

और master transform line: a sine of b x plus c, पूरे में plus d के लिए, amplitude है a का size, period two pi over b का size, phase shift minus c over b, और range d minus a का size से d plus a का size तक.
किसी भी trig graph को पढ़ने या sketch करने का पूरा reference यहाँ है.
Base periods: sine, cosine, secant और cosecant सब two pi पर दोहराते; tangent और cotangent pi पर दोहराते.
Scaling rule: function of b x plus c का period है base period बटा b का आकार. Constant c सिर्फ़ graph खिसकाता है, period कभी नहीं बदलता.
उन विचारों को पक्का करने के लिए tangent graph: branches के बीच period pi, vertical asymptotes odd multiples of pi बटा two पर, जहाँ cosine zero है.
अब वे composites जहाँ students फँसते हैं.
Sine और cosine के absolute values, और sine squared और cosine squared, सबका period pi है, two pi नहीं. और functions के sum के लिए, period है individual periods का least common multiple.
Asymptotes के लिए: tangent और secant वहाँ blow up होते हैं जहाँ cosine zero है, odd multiples of pi बटा two; cotangent और cosecant वहाँ जहाँ sine zero है, pi के whole multiples.

और master transform पंक्ति: a sine of b x plus c, पूरे में plus d के लिए, amplitude है a का आकार, period two pi बटा b का आकार, phase shift minus c बटा b, और range d minus a का आकार से d plus a का आकार तक.

sections.title: Periods, ranges and amplitudes

board_events.text: Example 1 — read off three periods
Example 2 — range and period of 3 + 2 sin x
Amplitude $2$, vertical shift $3$: range $=[3-2,\,3+2]=[1,5]$. The $\sin x$ is unscaled, so period $2\pi$.
Example 3 — amplitude and period of −4 cos(x/3)
The minus flips the graph vertically but changes neither amplitude nor period.

segments.text: Three quick reads to make the scaling rule automatic.

For the periods: sine three x divides two pi by three, giving two pi over three. Tangent two x uses the tangent base pi over two, so pi over two. And cosine of x over two divides two pi by one half, which is four pi, a stretched, slower wave.
Second, the range and period of three plus two sine x.
The amplitude is two and the vertical shift is three, so the range is three minus two to three plus two, that is one to five. The x inside sine is unscaled, so the period is just two pi.
Third, the amplitude and period of minus four cosine of x over three.
Amplitude is the size of minus four, which is four. Period is two pi over one third, which is six pi.
Notice the minus sign flips the graph upside down, but it touches neither the amplitude nor the period, both come from sizes only.
Scaling rule automatic करने के लिए तीन quick reads.

Periods के लिए: sine three x, two pi को three से divide, यानी two pi over three. Tangent two x tangent base pi over two use करता है, so pi over two. और cosine of x over two, two pi को one half से divide, यानी four pi, एक stretched, धीमी wave.
दूसरा, three plus two sine x का range और period.
Amplitude two और vertical shift three, so range है three minus two से three plus two, यानी one to five. Sine के अंदर x unscaled है, so period बस two pi.
तीसरा, minus four cosine of x over three का amplitude और period.
Amplitude है minus four का size, यानी four. Period है two pi over one third, यानी six pi.
ध्यान दीजिए minus sign graph को उल्टा flip करता है, पर ना amplitude ना period को छूता है, दोनों सिर्फ़ sizes से आते हैं.
Scaling rule स्वतः करने के लिए तीन quick reads.

Periods के लिए: sine three x, two pi को three से भाग, यानी two pi बटा three. Tangent two x tangent base pi बटा two use करता है, तो pi बटा two. और cosine of x बटा two, two pi को one half से भाग, यानी four pi, एक खिंची हुई, धीमी wave.
दूसरा, three plus two sine x का range और period.
Amplitude two और vertical shift three, तो range है three minus two से three plus two, यानी one से five. Sine के अंदर x unscaled है, तो period बस two pi.
तीसरा, minus four cosine of x बटा three का amplitude और period.
Amplitude है minus four का आकार, यानी four. Period है two pi बटा one third, यानी six pi.
ध्यान दीजिए minus चिह्न graph को उल्टा कर देता है, पर न amplitude न period को छूता है, दोनों सिर्फ़ आकार से आते हैं.

sections.subtopic: 04 · Graphs and Periodicity of Trigonometric Functions
sections.title: Composite and identity periods

board_events.text: Example 4 — period of |sin x| + |cos x|
Each of $|\sin x|,|\cos x|$ has period $\pi$. But $|\cos x|=|\sin(x+\tfrac{\pi}{2})|$, so the sum repeats sooner.
A hidden shrink: the sum's period is smaller than either part. Don't just take the larger.
Example 5 — period of sin²x
So $\sin^2 x$ has period $\pi$, not $2\pi$ \u2014 squaring halves the period here.

segments.text: These two show that periods can shrink in ways you must watch for.

Take the absolute value of sine x plus the absolute value of cosine x. Each absolute value on its own has period pi. But the absolute value of cosine x is the same as the absolute value of sine of x plus pi over two, so the two swap roles.
Push x forward by pi over two and the sum returns to itself: it becomes absolute cosine plus absolute sine, exactly f of x again. No smaller shift works, so the period is pi over two.
This is a hidden shrink. The sum repeats faster than either piece alone, so never just take the larger of the two periods, check carefully.
Example five: the period of sine squared x.
Use the power-reduction identity: sine squared x equals one minus cosine two x, all over two. The only moving part is cosine two x, which has period two pi over two, that is pi.
So sine squared x has period pi, not two pi. Squaring the sine has quietly halved its period.
ये दोनों दिखाते हैं कि periods ऐसे तरीक़ों से shrink हो सकते हैं जिनका ध्यान ज़रूरी है.

Absolute value of sine x plus absolute value of cosine x लीजिए. हर absolute value अकेले का period pi है. पर absolute value of cosine x वही है जो absolute value of sine of x plus pi over two, so दोनों roles swap कर लेते हैं.
x को pi over two आगे बढ़ाइए और sum ख़ुद पर लौट आता है: बनता है absolute cosine plus absolute sine, फिर exactly f of x. इससे छोटा shift काम नहीं करता, so period pi over two.
ये hidden shrink है. Sum किसी भी अकेले piece से तेज़ repeat होता है, so कभी सिर्फ़ बड़ा वाला period मत लीजिए, ध्यान से check कीजिए.
Example पाँच: sine squared x का period.
Power-reduction identity use कीजिए: sine squared x equals one minus cosine two x, पूरे over two. एकमात्र moving part है cosine two x, जिसका period two pi over two, यानी pi.
So sine squared x का period pi है, two pi नहीं. Sine को square करने ने चुपचाप उसका period आधा कर दिया.
ये दोनों दिखाते हैं कि periods ऐसे तरीक़ों से छोटे हो सकते हैं जिनका ध्यान ज़रूरी है.

Absolute value of sine x plus absolute value of cosine x लीजिए. हर absolute value अकेले का period pi है. पर absolute value of cosine x वही है जो absolute value of sine of x plus pi बटा two, तो दोनों की भूमिकाएँ बदल जाती हैं.
x को pi बटा two आगे बढ़ाइए और sum ख़ुद पर लौट आता है: बनता है absolute cosine plus absolute sine, फिर ठीक f of x. इससे छोटा shift काम नहीं करता, तो period pi बटा two.
यह छिपा हुआ shrink है. Sum किसी भी अकेले हिस्से से तेज़ दोहराता है, तो कभी सिर्फ़ बड़ा वाला period मत लीजिए, ध्यान से जाँचिए.
Example पाँच: sine squared x का period.
Power-reduction identity use कीजिए: sine squared x बराबर one minus cosine two x, पूरे बटा two. एकमात्र चलने वाला हिस्सा है cosine two x, जिसका period two pi बटा two, यानी pi.
तो sine squared x का period pi है, two pi नहीं. Sine को square करने ने चुपचाप उसका period आधा कर दिया.

sections.subtopic: 04 · Graphs and Periodicity of Trigonometric Functions
sections.title: Counting solutions and reading an inequality off the graph

board_events.text: Example 6 — how many solutions of |sin x| = |cos x| in [0, 2π]?
$|\sin x|=|\cos x| \iff |\tan x|=1$, the four points where the two 'tent' graphs cross.
Example 7 — solve sin x ≥ 1/2 on [0, 2π]
Draw the line $y=\tfrac12$ and shade where the sine curve sits on or above it, between its two crossings.
General solution: x ∈ [2nπ + π/6, 2nπ + 5π/6], n an integer.

segments.text: Graphs are the fastest way to count solutions and solve inequalities.
How many x in zero to two pi satisfy absolute sine equals absolute cosine? Divide through and it becomes the absolute value of tangent equals one, the points where the two tent-shaped graphs cross.
Those are pi over four, three pi over four, five pi over four, and seven pi over four, four solutions in one lap.
Example seven, an inequality: solve sine x at least one half on zero to two pi.
Draw the horizontal line y equals one half, and shade every place the sine curve sits on or above it. That's the stretch between its two crossing points.
Reading it off, x runs from pi over six to five pi over six, inclusive.
And by periodicity the general answer repeats every full turn: x lies between two n pi plus pi over six and two n pi plus five pi over six, for any integer n.
Graphs solutions गिनने और inequalities solve करने का सबसे तेज़ तरीक़ा हैं.
Zero से two pi में कितने x satisfy करते हैं absolute sine equals absolute cosine? Divide कीजिए और बनता है absolute value of tangent equals one, वो points जहाँ दोनों tent-shaped graphs cross करते हैं.
वो हैं pi over four, three pi over four, five pi over four, और seven pi over four, एक lap में four solutions.
Example सात, एक inequality: solve कीजिए sine x कम से कम one half, zero से two pi पर.
Horizontal line y equals one half खींचिए, और हर वो जगह shade कीजिए जहाँ sine curve उस पर या ऊपर बैठा है. वो है इसके दो crossing points के बीच का हिस्सा.
पढ़ने पर, x चलता है pi over six से five pi over six तक, दोनों शामिल.
और periodicity से general answer हर full turn पर repeat: x होता है two n pi plus pi over six और two n pi plus five pi over six के बीच, किसी भी integer n के लिए.
Graphs solutions गिनने और inequalities हल करने का सबसे तेज़ तरीक़ा हैं.
Zero से two pi में कितने x satisfy करते हैं absolute sine बराबर absolute cosine? Divide कीजिए और बनता है absolute value of tangent बराबर one, वे points जहाँ दोनों tent-shaped graphs मिलते हैं.
वे हैं pi बटा four, three pi बटा four, five pi बटा four, और seven pi बटा four, एक lap में four solutions.
Example सात, एक inequality: हल कीजिए sine x कम से कम one half, zero से two pi पर.

sections.title: Pitfalls with periods, ranges and asymptotes

board_events.text: Graph and period traps
#1 Signature trap: multiplying instead of dividing for the period. sin(bx) has period 2π/|b|, not 2π·b. Bigger b means shorter period.
#2 Using $2\pi$ for tangent. $\tan$ and $\cot$ have base period $\pi$.
#3 Period of a sum is the LCM of the parts — and watch for a hidden shrink, as in |sin x| + |cos x|.
#4 Forgetting the vertical shift in the range. Range of $a\sin x + d$ is $[d-|a|,\,d+|a|]$, not $[-|a|,|a|]$.
#5 Swapping asymptotes: $\tan,\sec$ blow up at odd $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$; $\cot,\csc$ at $n\pi$. #6 Decide open vs closed endpoints by whether the inequality is strict.
Golden rule: divide (don't multiply) for period; tangent's period is π.

segments.text: Six traps that decide the graph and period marks.
The signature trap: multiplying when you should divide. Sine of b x has period two pi over the size of b, not two pi times b. A bigger b means a shorter period, more waves squeezed in.
Second, using two pi for tangent. Tangent and cotangent have base period pi, half of the others.
Third, the period of a sum is the least common multiple of the parts, and stay alert for a hidden shrink like absolute sine plus absolute cosine, which drops all the way to pi over two.
Fourth, forgetting the vertical shift in the range. The range of a sine x plus d is d minus the size of a to d plus the size of a, not simply minus the size of a to the size of a.

Fifth, swapping asymptote locations. Tangent and secant blow up at the odd multiples of pi over two; cotangent and cosecant at the whole multiples of pi. And sixth, decide open versus closed endpoints by whether the inequality is strict.
The golden rule to carry: divide, never multiply, when finding a period, and remember tangent's period is pi.

Signature trap: divide करने की जगह multiply करना. Sine of b x का period है two pi over b का size, two pi times b नहीं. बड़ा b मतलब छोटा period, ज़्यादा waves ठुँसे हुए.
दूसरा, tangent के लिए two pi use करना. Tangent और cotangent का base period pi है, बाकी का आधा.
तीसरा, sum का period parts का least common multiple है, और hidden shrink के लिए alert रहिए जैसे absolute sine plus absolute cosine, जो सीधे pi over two तक गिर जाता है.
चौथा, range में vertical shift भूलना. a sine x plus d का range है d minus a का size से d plus a का size तक, सिर्फ़ minus a का size से a का size तक नहीं.

पाँचवाँ, asymptote locations swap करना. Tangent और secant odd multiples of pi over two पर blow up; cotangent और cosecant pi के whole multiples पर. और छठा, open versus closed endpoints तय कीजिए इस आधार पर कि inequality strict है या नहीं.
Golden rule साथ रखिए: period निकालते समय divide, कभी multiply नहीं, और याद रखिए tangent का period pi है.

sections.title: What a compound angle means — and why sin doesn't distribute

board_events.text: A compound angle is built from two others
$A+B$ or $A-B$. The naive guess $\sin(A+B)=\sin A+\sin B$ is flatly wrong.
Trig functions are not linear — they never distribute over a sum. This is the deepest error to kill early.
Two pushes combine into one
A sideways push $a\cos x$ and a forward push $b\sin x$ add to a single push of strength $R$ in one direction.

board_events.latex: a\cos x + b\sin x = R\cos(x-\alpha),\quad R=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}

board_events.text: So the maximum is $+R$ and the minimum is $-R$ \u2014 no calculus needed.

segments.text: Before the catalogue, let's be clear what a compound angle even is, and what it is not.
It's just an angle built from two others, A plus B or A minus B. And the tempting guess, that sine of A plus B equals sine A plus sine B, is simply false.
Test it: let A and B both be thirty degrees. Sine of sixty is root three over two, about zero point eight seven. But sine thirty plus sine thirty is one half plus one half, which is one. Not equal.
The lesson is deep: trig functions are not linear, they never distribute over a sum. Kill this instinct early and you avoid the most common error in the whole chapter.
Here's the intuition for the amplitude form, which we'll lean on.
Push a swing partly sideways, a cosine x, and partly forward, b sine x. The two combine into one single push, of strength R, in one combined direction.
That is, a cosine x plus b sine x equals R cosine of x minus alpha, where R is the square root of a squared plus b squared.
And because a cosine ranges between plus and minus one, the maximum of the whole thing is plus R and the minimum is minus R, no calculus required.
Catalogue से पहले, साफ़ कर लें compound angle है क्या, और क्या नहीं.
ये बस दो और angles से बना angle है, A plus B या A minus B. और tempting guess, कि sine of A plus B equals sine A plus sine B, बस ग़लत है.

सबक गहरा है: trig functions linear नहीं हैं, वो sum पर कभी distribute नहीं करतीं. इस instinct को जल्दी मार दीजिए और पूरे chapter की सबसे common ग़लती से बच जाइए.

sections.title: Sum and difference formulas, with the sign mnemonic

board_events.text: Compound angle: sum and difference
Sign mnemonic: cosine flips the sign, sine follows the sign, tangent's denominator is opposite the numerator.

board_events.caption: cos(A−B): equal chords on the unit circle give the master formula

board_events.text: Useful products of compound angles

segments.text: Here's the first block of the catalogue, the sum and difference formulas.
For cosine of A plus or minus B: cosine A cosine B, then minus or plus sine A sine B. The sign is opposite to the one inside.
For sine of A plus or minus B: sine A cosine B, then plus or minus cosine A sine B. The sign matches the one inside.
For tangent of A plus or minus B: tangent A plus or minus tangent B, all over one minus or plus tangent A tangent B.
One clean mnemonic ties them: cosine flips the sign, sine follows the sign, and for tangent the denominator's sign is opposite the numerator's.

And this is where the master formula comes from, geometrically: two equal chords on the unit circle, one spanning A to B and one spanning A minus B back to the point one, zero. Equal central angles force equal chords, and equating their squared lengths gives cosine of A minus B.
Two products worth memorising.
Cosine of A plus B times cosine of A minus B equals cosine squared A minus sine squared B.
And sine of A plus B times sine of A minus B equals sine squared A minus sine squared B.
Catalogue का पहला block, sum और difference formulas.
Cosine of A plus or minus B के लिए: cosine A cosine B, फिर minus या plus sine A sine B. Sign अंदर वाले के opposite है.
Sine of A plus or minus B के लिए: sine A cosine B, फिर plus या minus cosine A sine B. Sign अंदर वाले से match करता है.
Tangent of A plus or minus B के लिए: tangent A plus or minus tangent B, पूरे over one minus या plus tangent A tangent B.
एक clean mnemonic इन्हें जोड़ता है: cosine sign flip करता है, sine sign follow करता है, और tangent में denominator का sign numerator के opposite होता है.

और master formula यहीं से आता है, geometrically: unit circle पर दो equal chords, एक A से B तक और एक A minus B से वापस point one, zero तक. Equal central angles equal chords force करते हैं, और उनकी squared lengths बराबर करने से मिलता है cosine of A minus B.
दो products याद रखने लायक़.

sections.title: Double, half, triple and the t-substitution

board_events.text: Double-angle
Half-angle / power reduction
The t = tan(A/2) substitution

segments.text: Set B equal to A in the sum formulas and the double-angle family drops out.
Sine two A is two sine A cosine A, and tangent two A is two tangent A over one minus tangent squared A.
Cosine two A has three faces: cosine squared A minus sine squared A, or two cosine squared A minus one, or one minus two sine squared A. Choose whichever matches what you're given.
Rearranging cosine two A gives the half-angle, or power-reduction, forms.

First, cosine fifteen. Write fifteen as forty five minus thirty, and use the cosine difference formula: cosine forty five cosine thirty plus sine forty five sine thirty. Second, a proof: show cosine of A plus B times cosine of A minus B equals cosine squared A minus sine squared B. The product is a difference of squares, cosine squared A cosine squared B minus sine squared A sine squared B.
Now substitute cosine squared B as one minus sine squared B, and sine squared A as one minus cosine squared A. Expand and everything cancels down to cosine squared A minus sine squared B. Proved.

The trick is deliberate: multiply and divide by twice sine twenty, then cascade the double-angle identity, twice sine theta cosine theta is sine two theta.

Example eight is a conditional identity in a triangle: given A plus B plus C is pi, prove the sum of tangents equals the product.

From A plus B equals pi minus C, take tangents: tangent of A plus B is minus tangent C, so the sum formula gives tangent A plus tangent B, over one minus tangent A tangent B, equal to minus tangent C.

board_events.text: Identity traps
#1 Signature trap: the cosine/tangent sign flip. cos(A+B) takes minus; cos(A−B) takes plus. Cosine disagrees with the angle sign; sine agrees.
#2 Assuming distribution: $\sin(A+B)\ne\sin A+\sin B$. Always use the formula.
#3 Wrong $\cos 2A$ form. Given $\sin A$ use $1-2\sin^2 A$; given $\cos A$ use $2\cos^2 A-1$.
#4 Dropping the leading 2 in product-to-sum, and the leading minus in cos C − cos D.
#5 Amplitude is $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, never $a+b$. #6 Conditional identities hold only when A + B + C = \u03c0.
Golden rule: reconstruct from cos(A−B); watch every ±; amplitude is √(a²+b²).

segments.text: Six traps in the engine room, mostly structural, not arithmetic.

The signature trap: the sign flip in cosine and tangent. Cosine of A plus B takes a minus, cosine of A minus B takes a plus, so cosine disagrees with the angle's sign. Sine, by contrast, agrees. Get this backwards and everything downstream breaks.
Second, assuming distribution. Sine of A plus B is not sine A plus sine B. Trig functions are not linear, always reach for the formula.
Third, picking the wrong face of cosine two A. If you're given sine A, use one minus two sine squared A; if given cosine A, use two cosine squared A minus one. Match the form to what you have.
Fourth, dropping little pieces: the leading two in the product-to-sum formulas, and the leading minus in cosine C minus cosine D. Both are part of the formula.

Fifth, the amplitude of a sine plus b cosine is the square root of a squared plus b squared, never a plus b. And sixth, conditional identities like the tangent sum only hold when A plus B plus C is pi.
The golden rule: reconstruct everything from cosine of A minus B, watch every plus-or-minus, and remember the amplitude is root a squared plus b squared.
Engine room में छह traps, ज़्यादातर structural, arithmetic नहीं.

Signature trap: cosine और tangent में sign flip. Cosine of A plus B minus लेता है, cosine of A minus B plus लेता है, so cosine angle के sign से disagree करता है. Sine, इसके उलट, agree करता है. इसे उल्टा किया तो आगे सब टूट जाता है.
दूसरा, distribution मानना. Sine of A plus B, sine A plus sine B नहीं है. Trig functions linear नहीं, हमेशा formula उठाइए.

चौथा, छोटे टुकड़े छोड़ना: product-to-sum में leading two, और cosine C minus cosine D में leading minus. दोनों formula का हिस्सा हैं.

board_events.text: Losing roots by dividing
If you cancel $\cos\theta$ from $\sin\theta\cos\theta=\cos\theta$, you silently throw away every solution where $\cos\theta=0$.
Cancelling assumes the thing you cancel is non-zero — but here it can be zero. Factor, never divide.
Gaining roots by squaring
Squaring both sides can make a false equation look true, since $(-1)^2=1^2$.

board_events.latex: \sin x + \cos x = 1 \xrightarrow{\text{square}} \sin 2x = 0,\ \text{but } x=\pi \text{ fails the original}

board_events.text: Every solution from a squared equation must be checked back in the original.
These two are the signature traps — both are conceptual gaps, not careless slips.

segments.text: Two dangers cause almost every wrong answer in this subtopic, and both are conceptual.
The first is losing roots by dividing. Suppose you have sine theta cosine theta equals cosine theta, and you cancel cosine theta from both sides.
The moment you cancel, you silently throw away every solution where cosine theta is zero.
Cancelling secretly assumes the thing you cancel is non-zero. But here it can be zero, that's exactly the case you just deleted. So factor, and set each factor to zero, never divide.
The second danger is gaining roots by squaring. Squaring both sides can make a false statement look true, because minus one squared equals one squared.

Watch: sine x plus cosine x equals one. Square it and you get sine two x equals zero, which includes x equal to pi. But sine pi plus cosine pi is minus one, not one, so x equal to pi is a fake, an extraneous root.
So every candidate that comes out of a squared equation must be checked back in the original, and the fakes discarded.
These are the two signature traps of the whole subtopic, and notice, they're gaps in understanding, not careless arithmetic.

पहला है divide करके roots खोना. मान लीजिए sine theta cosine theta equals cosine theta है, और आप दोनों तरफ़ से cosine theta cancel कर देते हैं.
जिस पल आप cancel करते हैं, आप चुपचाप हर वो solution फेंक देते हैं जहाँ cosine theta zero है.
Cancel करना चुपके से मानता है कि जो cancel कर रहे हैं वो non-zero है. पर यहाँ वो zero हो सकता है, यही case आपने अभी delete किया. So factor कीजिए, हर factor को zero रखिए, divide कभी नहीं.
दूसरा danger है square करके roots पाना. दोनों तरफ़ square करना झूठे statement को सच दिखा सकता है, क्योंकि minus one squared equals one squared.

So squared equation से निकला हर candidate original में check होना चाहिए, और नक़ली हटा दीजिए.

segments.text: Here is the short, fixed list that solves the whole subtopic. Start with the zero cases.
Sine theta is zero at whole multiples of pi; cosine theta at odd multiples of pi over two; tangent theta at whole multiples of pi.
Now the three master general solutions, one per function.
For sine theta equals sine alpha: theta is n pi plus minus one to the n, times alpha.
For cosine theta equals cosine alpha: theta is two n pi plus or minus alpha; and for tangent theta equals tangent alpha: theta is n pi plus alpha. Never borrow another function's form.
One more covers all squared cases: sine squared, cosine squared, or tangent squared equal to the same of alpha gives theta equals n pi plus or minus alpha.
Then the linear form and its solvability test.

Rewrite a cosine theta plus b sine theta as R cosine of theta minus alpha equals c; it's solvable only if the size of c is at most the square root of a squared plus b squared, otherwise there is no solution.

And run the root-validity checklist every time: keep the integer n, restore any roots lost to division, back-check every candidate after squaring, and drop any out-of-domain root. Throughout, n is an integer.

segments.text: Three foundational solves.

First, principal solutions of sine x equals one half. Sine is positive in the first and second quadrants, so within one lap we get x equals pi over six, and x equals pi minus pi over six, which is five pi over six.
Second, the general solution of cosine x equals minus one half. Minus one half is cosine of two pi over three, so by the cosine formula, x equals two n pi plus or minus two pi over three.
Third, a quadratic in sine x: two sine squared x plus sine x minus one equals zero.
Treat sine x as the variable and factor: two sine x minus one, times sine x plus one, equals zero. So sine x is one half, or sine x is minus one.
From sine x equals one half, x is n pi plus minus one to the n times pi over six. From sine x equals minus one, x is four n minus one, times pi over two.
The habit to build: reduce every equation to sine equals sine, cosine equals cosine, or tangent equals tangent, then just quote the matching master formula.

तीसरा, sine x में एक quadratic: two sine squared x plus sine x minus one equals zero.
Sine x को variable मानकर factor कीजिए: two sine x minus one, times sine x plus one, equals zero. So sine x है one half, या sine x है minus one.

board_events.text: Example 4 — solve √3 cos x + sin x = 1
$R=\sqrt{3+1}=2$, $\tan\alpha=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\Rightarrow\alpha=\tfrac{\pi}{6}$. So $\cos(x-\tfrac{\pi}{6})=\tfrac12=\cos\tfrac{\pi}{3}$.
Example 5 — factor, don't divide: sin 2x = sin x
$\sin x = 0 \Rightarrow x=n\pi$; $\cos x=\tfrac12 \Rightarrow x=2n\pi\pm\tfrac{\pi}{3}$.
Dividing by sin x would erase the entire x = nπ family — the signature trap.

segments.text: Two workhorses: the linear form and the factor-don't-divide discipline.

Example four: solve root three cosine x plus sine x equals one. Here a is root three and b is one, so R is the square root of three plus one, which is two, and tangent alpha is one over root three, so alpha is pi over six.
Rewrite as two cosine of x minus pi over six equals one, that is cosine of x minus pi over six equals one half, which is cosine pi over three.

So x minus pi over six equals two n pi plus or minus pi over three, giving x equals two n pi plus pi over two, or x equals two n pi minus pi over six. And the size of c, one, is at most R, two, so solutions do exist.

Example five drives home factoring. Solve sine two x equals sine x. Move everything over: two sine x cosine x minus sine x equals zero, then factor out sine x to get sine x times two cosine x minus one equals zero.
So either sine x is zero, giving x equals n pi, or cosine x is one half, giving x equals two n pi plus or minus pi over three.
If instead you had divided both sides by sine x, you would have erased the entire x equals n pi family. That is the signature trap, factor, never divide.
दो workhorses: linear form और factor-don't-divide discipline.

Example चार: solve कीजिए root three cosine x plus sine x equals one. यहाँ a है root three और b one, so R है square root of three plus one, यानी two, और tangent alpha है one over root three, so alpha है pi over six.
फिर से लिखिए two cosine of x minus pi over six equals one, यानी cosine of x minus pi over six equals one half, जो cosine pi over three है.

So x minus pi over six equals two n pi plus or minus pi over three, देता x equals two n pi plus pi over two, या x equals two n pi minus pi over six. और c का size, one, R यानी two से ज़्यादा नहीं, so solutions मौजूद हैं.

Example पाँच factoring पक्का करता है. Solve कीजिए sine two x equals sine x. सब एक तरफ़ लाइए: two sine x cosine x minus sine x equals zero, फिर sine x बाहर factor कीजिए, मिलता sine x times two cosine x minus one equals zero.
So या तो sine x zero है, देता x equals n pi, या cosine x one half है, देता x equals two n pi plus or minus pi over three.
अगर इसके बजाय आपने दोनों तरफ़ sine x से divide किया होता, आप पूरी x equals n pi family मिटा देते. यही signature trap है, factor, divide कभी नहीं.
दो workhorses: linear form और factor-don't-divide अनुशासन.

Example चार: हल कीजिए root three cosine x plus sine x बराबर one. यहाँ a है root three और b one, तो R है square root of three plus one, यानी two, और tangent alpha है one बटा root three, तो alpha है pi बटा six.
फिर से लिखिए two cosine of x minus pi बटा six बराबर one, यानी cosine of x minus pi बटा six बराबर one half, जो cosine pi बटा three है.

तो x minus pi बटा six बराबर two n pi plus या minus pi बटा three, देता x बराबर two n pi plus pi बटा two, या x बराबर two n pi minus pi बटा six. और c का आकार, one, R यानी two से ज़्यादा नहीं, तो solutions मौजूद हैं.

Example पाँच factoring पक्का करता है. हल कीजिए sine two x बराबर sine x. सब एक ओर लाइए: two sine x cosine x minus sine x बराबर zero, फिर sine x बाहर factor कीजिए, मिलता sine x गुणा two cosine x minus one बराबर zero.
तो या तो sine x zero है, देता x बराबर n pi, या cosine x one half है, देता x बराबर two n pi plus या minus pi बटा three.
अगर इसके बजाय आपने दोनों ओर sine x से भाग किया होता, आप पूरी x बराबर n pi family मिटा देते. यही signature trap है, factor, भाग कभी नहीं.

sections.title: The squaring trap done right, and a range squeeze

board_events.text: Example 6 — solve sin x + cos x = 1 (without squaring)
Amplitude form: $\sin x+\cos x=\sqrt2\,\sin(x+\tfrac{\pi}{4})$, so $\sin(x+\tfrac{\pi}{4})=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=\sin\tfrac{\pi}{4}$.
Squaring instead gives sin 2x = 0, which admits x = π — but sinπ + cosπ = −1. Back-checking removes it.
Example 7 — range squeeze: 2sin²x + sin²2x = 2
With $\sin^2 2x = 4\sin^2 x\cos^2 x$ and $s=\sin^2 x$: $2s+4s(1-s)=2 \Rightarrow (2s-1)(s-1)=0$.

segments.text: The finale: how to beat the squaring trap, and a neat substitution.

Example six: solve sine x plus cosine x equals one. The safe route avoids squaring entirely, use the amplitude form. Sine x plus cosine x is root two times sine of x plus pi over four, so sine of x plus pi over four equals one over root two, which is sine pi over four.
Solving that gives x equals two n pi, or x equals two n pi plus pi over two. Clean, with no fakes.

Contrast the squaring route: square the original and you get sine two x equals zero, which admits x equal to pi. But sine pi plus cosine pi is minus one, not one, so pi is extraneous. Only back-checking removes it, which is why the amplitude form is safer.
Example seven, a range squeeze: two sine squared x plus sine squared two x equals two.

Write sine squared two x as four sine squared x cosine squared x, and let s be sine squared x. Then two s plus four s times one minus s equals two, which tidies to two s minus one, times s minus one, equals zero.

So s is one half or s is one. Sine squared x equals one half gives x equals n pi plus or minus pi over four; sine squared x equals one means cosine x is zero, giving x equals two n plus one, times pi over two.
Finale: squaring trap को कैसे हराएँ, और एक neat substitution.

Example छह: solve कीजिए sine x plus cosine x equals one. Safe route squaring से पूरी तरह बचता है, amplitude form use कीजिए. Sine x plus cosine x है root two times sine of x plus pi over four, so sine of x plus pi over four equals one over root two, जो sine pi over four है.
इसे solve करने पर x equals two n pi, या x equals two n pi plus pi over two. साफ़, कोई नक़ली नहीं.

Squaring route से तुलना: original को square कीजिए और मिलता sine two x equals zero, जिसमें x equal to pi है. पर sine pi plus cosine pi है minus one, one नहीं, so pi extraneous है. सिर्फ़ back-checking इसे हटाता है, इसीलिए amplitude form safer है.
Example सात, एक range squeeze: two sine squared x plus sine squared two x equals two.

Sine squared two x को four sine squared x cosine squared x लिखिए, और s को sine squared x लीजिए. तो two s plus four s times one minus s equals two, जो साफ़ होकर two s minus one, times s minus one, equals zero बनता है.

So s है one half या s है one. Sine squared x equals one half देता x equals n pi plus or minus pi over four; sine squared x equals one मतलब cosine x zero, देता x equals two n plus one, times pi over two.
Finale: squaring trap को कैसे हराएँ, और एक neat substitution.

Example छह: हल कीजिए sine x plus cosine x बराबर one. Safe route squaring से पूरी तरह बचता है, amplitude form use कीजिए. Sine x plus cosine x है root two गुणा sine of x plus pi बटा four, तो sine of x plus pi बटा four बराबर one बटा root two, जो sine pi बटा four है.
इसे हल करने पर x बराबर two n pi, या x बराबर two n pi plus pi बटा two. साफ़, कोई नक़ली नहीं.

Example सात, एक range squeeze: two sine squared x plus sine squared two x बराबर two.

Sine squared two x को four sine squared x cosine squared x लिखिए, और s को sine squared x लीजिए. तो two s plus four s गुणा one minus s बराबर two, जो साफ़ होकर two s minus one, गुणा s minus one, बराबर zero बनता है.
तो s है one half या s है one. Sine squared x बराबर one half देता x बराबर n pi plus या minus pi बटा four; sine squared x बराबर one मतलब cosine x zero, देता x बराबर two n plus one, गुणा pi बटा two.

sections.title: Pitfalls in solving trig equations

board_events.text: Equation traps
#1 Signature trap: dividing by a trig factor and losing roots. Never cancel sin x or cos x — factor and set each factor to zero.
#2 Squaring and keeping extraneous roots. Every candidate from a squared step must be checked in the original equation.
#3 Mixing the families. Sine: $n\pi+(-1)^n\alpha$; cosine: $2n\pi\pm\alpha$; tangent: $n\pi+\alpha$. Never borrow another's form.
#4 Giving only principal solutions when 'general' is asked — the integer n is mandatory.
#5 Ignoring solvability: if $|c|>\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, declare 'no solution'. #6 Drop roots where tan, sec, cot or csc is undefined.
Golden rules: factor (never divide); back-check after squaring; keep the n; match the right family.

segments.text: Six traps that decide the equations marks.
The signature trap: dividing by a trig factor and losing roots. Never cancel sine x or cosine x, because the thing you cancel might be zero. Factor instead, and set each factor to zero.
Second, squaring and keeping extraneous roots. Squaring can manufacture false solutions, so every candidate that came through a squared step must be checked back in the original equation.

Third, mixing up the solution families. Sine gives n pi plus minus one to the n times alpha; cosine gives two n pi plus or minus alpha; tangent gives n pi plus alpha. Each function has its own form, never borrow another's.
Fourth, giving only principal solutions when the question asks for the general one. The integer n is mandatory; drop it and you lose infinitely many answers.

Fifth, ignoring solvability of the linear form. If the size of c exceeds the square root of a squared plus b squared, just declare no solution instead of grinding. And sixth, discard any root where tangent, secant, cotangent or cosecant is undefined.
The golden rules for the whole subtopic: factor, never divide; back-check after squaring; keep the n; and match the right family to the right function.

Signature trap: trig factor से divide करके roots खोना. Sine x या cosine x कभी cancel मत कीजिए, क्योंकि जो cancel कर रहे हैं वो zero हो सकता है. इसके बजाय factor कीजिए, और हर factor को zero रखिए.
दूसरा, square करके extraneous roots रखना. Squaring झूठे solutions बना सकता है, so squared step से आया हर candidate original equation में back-check होना चाहिए.

तीसरा, solution families mix करना. Sine देता n pi plus minus one to the n times alpha; cosine देता two n pi plus or minus alpha; tangent देता n pi plus alpha. हर function का अपना form, दूसरे का कभी उधार नहीं.
चौथा, सिर्फ़ principal solutions देना जब सवाल general माँगे. Integer n ज़रूरी है; छोड़िए और infinitely many answers खो जाते हैं.

पाँचवाँ, linear form की solvability ignore करना. अगर c का size square root of a squared plus b squared से ज़्यादा है, बस no solution घोषित कीजिए grind करने के बजाय. और छठा, जहाँ tangent, secant, cotangent या cosecant undefined हो वो root हटाइए.

board_events.text: Fast-recall golden rules
Angles: any arc / sector / calculus formula assumes radians. Convert first, always.
Functions: magnitude from the identity, sign from the quadrant — always two steps. Range-check every answer.
Allied angles: odd multiple of 90° ⇒ swap to co-function; sign from the quadrant via ASTC.
Graphs: divide (don't multiply) for the period; tangent's period is π; include the vertical shift in the range.
Identities: reconstruct everything from cos(A−B); watch every ±; amplitude is √(a²+b²), never a+b.
Equations: factor (never divide); back-check after squaring; keep the n; match the right solution family.
If a final sin or cos exceeds 1 in magnitude, or a period looks multiplied not divided — stop and recheck.
